topic.name: The Ant and the Cricket
topic.description: A fable poem adapted from Aesop, about a cricket who sang all summer instead of storing food, and an ant who refuses him shelter and grain when winter comes because the ants' own rule is never to borrow and never to lend.
topic.source_evidence: A fable is a story, Often with Animals तड Characters, that Conveys A moral. This poem about an ant and २ Cricket

concepts.name: Adapted from Aesop's Fables
concepts.description: The poem is not an original composition but a retelling of one of Aesop's fables, keeping the ant-and-cricket cast and the moral about preparing for hard times.
concepts.definition: The poem is adapted from Aesop's Fables.

concepts.name: A silly young cricket, accustomed to sing
concepts.description: The poet introduces the cricket as silly and young, and describes how he spent the warm months of summer and spring singing rather than working.
concepts.definition: The cricket is described as a silly young cricket, accustomed to singing through the warm, sunny months of summer and spring.
concepts.source_evidence: A Silly young Cricket, Accustomed ४० Sing Through the Warm

concepts.name: His cupboard was empty, and winter was come
concepts.description: The cricket begins to complain only once winter arrives and he finds he has nothing at home to eat -- the moment his carefree summer catches up with him.
concepts.definition: The cricket began to complain when he found that, at home, his cupboard was empty and winter had come.
concepts.source_evidence: At Home, His cupboard Was empty, and Winter Was Come

concepts.name: Famine: a scarcity of food
concepts.description: The poem's own glossary defines famine as a scarcity of food, having nothing to eat -- the word the cricket's starving winter is named by.
concepts.definition: Famine means a scarcity of food, having nothing to eat.
concepts.source_evidence: amine: Scarcity Of food having nothing to eat

concepts.name: A mouthful of grain, to be repaid tomorrow
concepts.description: Driven by hunger, the cricket goes to the ant to ask for shelter from the rain and a mouthful of grain, and says he only wishes to borrow it, promising to repay the ant the next day.
concepts.definition: The cricket asks the ant for shelter from rain and a mouthful of grain, wishing only to borrow it and repay it tomorrow.
concepts.source_evidence: He Wished Only to borrow He'd repay

concepts.name: Starvation and sorrow
concepts.description: The cricket tells the ant that if he is refused, he must die of starvation and sorrow -- the stakes he puts on the ant's answer.
concepts.definition: If the ant does not help him, the cricket says he must die of starvation and sorrow.
concepts.source_evidence: If not, he must die ०ि Starvation and Sorrow

concepts.name: We ants never borrow, we ants never lend
concepts.description: The ant answers first as a servant and friend, then states the ants' own rule -- they neither borrow nor lend -- before asking the cricket what he was doing all summer.
concepts.definition: The ant replies that he is the cricket's servant and friend, but that ants never borrow and never lend.
concepts.source_evidence: Says the ant ४० the cricket, I'm your Servant and friend, But We Ants Never borrow We Ants Never lend

concepts.name: Dance the winter away
concepts.description: Once the cricket admits he sang all summer instead of storing food, the ant's final answer is that he should dance the winter away instead -- and shuts the door on him.
concepts.definition: The ant tells the cricket that, since he sang all summer, he should dance the winter away.
